summary: Across UTI's 16 programs, close to 20,000 students hand in documents that instructors mark by hand. Instructors teach 8 to 10 hours a day and then spend another 3 to 4 hours marking, most of it in the evening. Blackboard Ultra's short answer autograding cannot carry this, because an answer that is one character off is counted as wrong. With roughly 1,500 instructors, this is a significant operating investment made by UTI. The marking burden is also one of the driving factors in instructor attrition; instructors earn more in the field, where they don’t have a marking burden in the evenings. Additionally, students only receive occasional verbal feedback, and this leads to a black box for education leadership. Consistent, structured written feedback across all UTI programs will have a positive impact on education quality for students, possibly leading to higher student retention and potentially more demand.

Eduface marks assignments inside Blackboard Ultra against answer keys, and writes feedback per criterion instead of only a score. The goal for UTI is to partly relieve instructors of their marking burden and to give students written feedback in Blackboard Ultra, where today that feedback is mostly verbal.
Our mutual aim is to Go Live in Blackboard Ultra with the first programs in January 2027. This document is the shared plan to get there, and both teams keep it up to date.
